obligations.summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models must provide the Commission with documentation drawn up under Articles 53 and 55, or any additional information necessary to assess compliance with the Regulation, when requested.
The AI Office may initiate a structured dialogue with the provider of a general-purpose AI model before sending a formal request for information.

Upon a duly substantiated request from the scientific panel, the Commission may issue a request for information to a provider of a general-purpose AI model where such access is necessary and proportionate for the scientific panel's tasks.
exceptions: Request must be duly substantiated by the scientific panel
Access to information must be necessary and proportionate for fulfilment of the scientific panel's tasks under Article 68(2)

obligations.summary: Any request for information issued by the Commission must state the legal basis and purpose, specify the information required, set a deadline for provision, and indicate the fines applicable under Article 101 for incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information.

Providers of general-purpose AI models, or their authorised legal representatives or lawyers, must supply the information requested by the Commission, with the client remaining fully responsible for the completeness and accuracy of information supplied on their behalf.
exceptions: Lawyers duly authorised to act may supply information on behalf of their clients, though clients remain fully responsible for incomplete, incorrect, or misleading information
